headline: How a Sushi Chain CEO Turned Pirates into Fishermen
meta_description: Kiyoshi Kimura, CEO of Sushizanmai, provided vessels and training to help former Somali pirates transition to legal fishing.
summary_short: A Japanese sushi entrepreneur transformed piracy networks by offering former pirates fishing vessels, training, and market access to earn sustainable livelihoods.
body:
Kiyoshi Kimura, CEO of the popular Japanese sushi chain Sushizanmai, helped dismantle piracy networks in Somalia by offering former pirates a legal alternative: fishing.

Rather than treating piracy as a security problem alone, Kimura recognized its root cause—economic desperation. He provided fishing vessels and comprehensive training to men who had turned to crime out of necessity. By connecting them to Sushizanmai's tuna distribution network, he created a pathway to sustainable income.

The initiative reveals how entrepreneurial thinking and genuine empathy can address complex international challenges. Kimura didn't simply donate; he built a system that gave former pirates dignity, skills, and real economic opportunity. What began as an unlikely intersection between Japanese business and Somali communities became a model for solving piracy through opportunity rather than force alone.
quick_facts: Kiyoshi Kimura is CEO of Sushizanmai, a major Japanese sushi chain
He provided fishing vessels and training to former Somali pirates
The initiative connected pirates to Sushizanmai's tuna distribution network
Approach focused on creating legal, sustainable livelihoods over enforcement
